claim: Two related multisubunit tethering complexes promote endolysosomal trafficking in all eukaryotes: Rab5-binding CORVET and Rab7-binding HOPS.
source: Two related multisubunit tethering complexes promote endolysosomal trafficking in all eukaryotes: Rab5-binding CORVET that was suggested to transform into Rab7-binding HOPS.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to established literature on CORVET and HOPS complexes.

claim: CORVET was suggested to transform into HOPS.
source: Two related multisubunit tethering complexes promote endolysosomal trafficking in all eukaryotes: Rab5-binding CORVET that was suggested to transform into Rab7-binding HOPS.
evidence: This is a hypothesis from prior literature that the authors are referencing.

claim: miniCORVET contains Drosophila Vps8 and three shared core proteins.
source: We have previously identified miniCORVET, containing Drosophila Vps8 and three shared core proteins, which are required for endosome maturation upstream of HOPS in highly endocytic cells (Lőrincz et al., 2016a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: miniCORVET is required for endosome maturation upstream of HOPS in highly endocytic cells.
source: We have previously identified miniCORVET, containing Drosophila Vps8 and three shared core proteins, which are required for endosome maturation upstream of HOPS in highly endocytic cells (Lőrincz et al., 2016a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Vps8 overexpression inhibits late endosome maturation.
source: Here, we show that Vps8 overexpression inhibits HOPS-dependent trafficking routes including late endosome maturation, autophagosome-lysosome fusion, crinophagy and lysosome-related organelle formation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including confocal and electron microscopy experiments.

claim: Vps8 overexpression inhibits autophagosome-lysosome fusion.
source: Here, we show that Vps8 overexpression inhibits HOPS-dependent trafficking routes including late endosome maturation, autophagosome-lysosome fusion, crinophagy and lysosome-related organelle formation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Vps8 overexpression inhibits crinophagy.
source: Here, we show that Vps8 overexpression inhibits HOPS-dependent trafficking routes including late endosome maturation, autophagosome-lysosome fusion, crinophagy and lysosome-related organelle formation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Vps8 overexpression inhibits lysosome-related organelle formation.
source: Here, we show that Vps8 overexpression inhibits HOPS-dependent trafficking routes including late endosome maturation, autophagosome-lysosome fusion, crinophagy and lysosome-related organelle formation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Vps8 overexpression abolishes the late endosomal localization of HOPS-specific Vps41/Lt.
source: Mechanistically, Vps8 overexpression abolishes the late endosomal localization of HOPS-specific Vps41/Lt and prevents HOPS assembly.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data showing loss of Vps41-9xHA signal on late endosomes upon Vps8 overexpression.

claim: Vps8 overexpression prevents HOPS assembly.
source: Mechanistically, Vps8 overexpression abolishes the late endosomal localization of HOPS-specific Vps41/Lt and prevents HOPS assembly.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data showing decreased amounts of HOPS complex upon Vps8 overexpression.

claim: Proper ratio of Vps8 to Vps41 is critical because Vps8 negatively regulates HOPS by outcompeting Vps41.
source: Proper ratio of Vps8 to Vps41 is thus critical because Vps8 negatively regulates HOPS by outcompeting Vps41.
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data and the observation that Vps8 overexpression phenocopies HOPS loss-of-function.

claim: Endosomal recruitment of miniCORVET-specific subunits requires proper complex assembly.
source: Endosomal recruitment of miniCORVET- or HOPS-specific subunits requires proper complex assembly, and Vps8/miniCORVET is dispensable for autophagy, crinophagy and lysosomal biogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that Vps8 localization depends on class C proteins.

claim: Endosomal recruitment of HOPS-specific subunits requires proper complex assembly.
source: Endosomal recruitment of miniCORVET- or HOPS-specific subunits requires proper complex assembly, and Vps8/miniCORVET is dispensable for autophagy, crinophagy and lysosomal biogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that Vps41 localization depends on all other HOPS subunits and class C proteins.

claim: Vps8/miniCORVET is dispensable for autophagy.
source: Endosomal recruitment of miniCORVET- or HOPS-specific subunits requires proper complex assembly, and Vps8/miniCORVET is dispensable for autophagy, crinophagy and lysosomal biogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAi and mutant data showing no effect of Vps8 loss on autophagy.

claim: Vps8/miniCORVET is dispensable for crinophagy.
source: Endosomal recruitment of miniCORVET- or HOPS-specific subunits requires proper complex assembly, and Vps8/miniCORVET is dispensable for autophagy, crinophagy and lysosomal biogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAi data showing no effect of Vps8 loss on crinophagy.

claim: Vps8/miniCORVET is dispensable for lysosomal biogenesis.
source: Endosomal recruitment of miniCORVET- or HOPS-specific subunits requires proper complex assembly, and Vps8/miniCORVET is dispensable for autophagy, crinophagy and lysosomal biogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing normal eye pigmentation in vps8 mutants.

claim: miniCORVET and HOPS are recruited to target membranes independent of each other in Drosophila.
source: These data together indicate the recruitment of these complexes to target membranes independent of each other in Drosophila, rather than their transformation during vesicle maturation.
evidence: This claim is based on the observation that HOPS is functional in the absence of miniCORVET and vice versa.

claim: miniCORVET and HOPS do not transform into each other during vesicle maturation in Drosophila.
source: These data together indicate the recruitment of these complexes to target membranes independent of each other in Drosophila, rather than their transformation during vesicle maturation.
evidence: This claim is based on the observation that the complexes function independently and no hybrid complexes were detected.

claim: HOPS was identified in yeast.
source: HOPS was identified in yeast and is defined by two Ypt7 (Rab7 in higher eukaryotes) binding subunits Vps41 and Vps39 on its opposing ends (Balderhaar et al., 2013; Balderhaar and Ungermann, 2013; Bröcker et al., 2012; Lürick et al., 2018; Peplowska et al., 2007; Plemel et al., 2011; Rieder and Emr, 1997; Seals et al., 2000; Wickner and Schekman, 2008; Wurmser et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: HOPS is defined by two Ypt7 (Rab7 in higher eukaryotes) binding subunits Vps41 and Vps39 on its opposing ends.
source: HOPS was identified in yeast and is defined by two Ypt7 (Rab7 in higher eukaryotes) binding subunits Vps41 and Vps39 on its opposing ends (Balderhaar et al., 2013; Balderhaar and Ungermann, 2013; Bröcker et al., 2012; Lürick et al., 2018; Peplowska et al., 2007; Plemel et al., 2011; Rieder and Emr, 1997; Seals et al., 2000; Wickner and Schekman, 2008; Wurmser et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: In metazoan cells including Drosophila, HOPS directly binds to Rab2 and Rab7-binding adaptors to ensure fusions of lysosomes with autophagosomes, late endosomes, secretory granules and Golgi derived vesicles.
source: In metazoan cells including Drosophila, HOPS directly binds to Rab2 and Rab7-binding adaptors to ensure fusions of lysosomes with autophagosomes, late endosomes, secretory granules and Golgi derived vesicles (Angers and Merz, 2009; Balderhaar and Ungermann, 2013; Csizmadia et al., 2018; Fujita et al., 2017; Jiang et al., 2014; Kajiho et al., 2016; Lőrincz et al., 2017b; McEwan et al., 2015; Pankiv et al., 2010; Pols et al., 2013a; Solinger and Spang, 2013; van der Kant et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: CORVET mediates the tethering and fusions of Vps21 (Rab5 in higher eukaryotes) positive membranes.
source: A closely related multisubunit complex termed CORVET (Class C core endosome vacuole tethering) mediates the tethering and fusions of Vps21 (Rab5 in higher eukaryotes) positive membranes (Balderhaar et al., 2013; Balderhaar and Ungermann, 2013; Bröcker et al., 2012; Lürick et al., 2018; Peplowska et al., 2007; Plemel et al., 2011; Rieder and Emr, 1997; Seals et al., 2000; Wurmser et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Both CORVET and HOPS share a common core of class C Vps proteins (Vps11, Vps16, Vps18 and Vps33).
source: Both CORVET and HOPS share a common core of class C Vps proteins (Vps11, Vps16, Vps18 and Vps33), but in the former complex two Vps21 (Rab5 in higher eukaryotes) binding subunits: Vps8 and Vps3 are present instead of the Ypt7/Rab7 binding Vps41 and Vps39, respectively (Balderhaar and Ungermann, 2013; Bröcker et al., 2012; Lürick et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: In CORVET, two Vps21 (Rab5 in higher eukaryotes) binding subunits Vps8 and Vps3 are present instead of the Ypt7/Rab7 binding Vps41 and Vps39.
source: Both CORVET and HOPS share a common core of class C Vps proteins (Vps11, Vps16, Vps18 and Vps33), but in the former complex two Vps21 (Rab5 in higher eukaryotes) binding subunits: Vps8 and Vps3 are present instead of the Ypt7/Rab7 binding Vps41 and Vps39, respectively (Balderhaar and Ungermann, 2013; Bröcker et al., 2012; Lürick et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: HOPS is conserved across metazoans.
source: Whilst HOPS is conserved across metazoans, higher eukaryotes lack Vps3, which is therefore yeast-specific.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of HOPS conservation.

claim: Higher eukaryotes lack Vps3, which is therefore yeast-specific.
source: Whilst HOPS is conserved across metazoans, higher eukaryotes lack Vps3, which is therefore yeast-specific.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of CORVET composition.

claim: Mammalian CORVET contains Vps39-2 (also known as Tgfbrap1 or Trap1) in the place of Vps3.
source: Mammalian CORVET contains Vps39-2 (also known as Tgfbrap1 or Trap1) in the place of Vps3, and Vps8 is conserved (Lachmann et al., 2014; Perini et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Vps8 is conserved in mammalian CORVET.
source: Mammalian CORVET contains Vps39-2 (also known as Tgfbrap1 or Trap1) in the place of Vps3, and Vps8 is conserved (Lachmann et al., 2014; Perini et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Drosophila has a smaller CORVET variant termed miniCORVET, containing Vps8 and only three of the four class C Vps proteins (Dor/Vps18, Car/Vps33A and Vps16A).
source: Drosophila has a smaller CORVET variant termed miniCORVET, containing Vps8 and only three of the four class C Vps proteins (Dor/Vps18, Car/Vps33A and Vps16A).
evidence: This claim is based on the authors' previous characterization of miniCORVET.

claim: Vps11 is a HOPS specific protein in flies.
source: Thus, Vps11 is a HOPS specific protein in flies (Lőrincz et al., 2016a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: In yeast, a series of biochemical experiments on overexpressed complex specific subunits suggested the existence of intermediate complexes that contain one CORVET and one HOPS specific Vps protein.
source: In yeast, a series of biochemical experiments on overexpressed complex specific subunits suggested the existence of intermediate complexes that contain one CORVET and one HOPS specific Vps protein (Peplowska et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Overexpression of CORVET specific subunits can disturb endosome maturation in yeast.
source: Moreover, overexpression of CORVET specific subunits can disturb endosome maturation and Vps3 can displace Vps39 from HOPS, potentially as a result of competition between complex specific subunits (Markgraf et al., 2009; Ostrowicz et al., 2010; Peplowska et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Vps3 can displace Vps39 from HOPS in yeast.
source: Moreover, overexpression of CORVET specific subunits can disturb endosome maturation and Vps3 can displace Vps39 from HOPS, potentially as a result of competition between complex specific subunits (Markgraf et al., 2009; Ostrowicz et al., 2010; Peplowska et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: During assembly, complex-specific proteins may compete for class C proteins in yeast.
source: These results raise the possibility that during assembly, complex-specific proteins may compete for class C proteins in yeast.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on yeast data cited in the manuscript.

claim: Drosophila is an excellent model to study miniCORVET and HOPS mediated vesicular trafficking processes.
source: Others and we have previously shown that Drosophila is an excellent model to study miniCORVET and HOPS mediated vesicular trafficking processes, including endosome maturation in nephrocytes, autophagosome-lysosome fusion in fat cells, crinophagy in salivary glands and eye pigment granule biogenesis (Akbar et al., 2009; Csizmadia et al., 2018; Lindmo et al., 2006; Lőrincz et al., 2016a; Lőrincz et al., 2017a; Lőrincz et al., 2016b; Lőrincz et al., 2017b; Pulipparacharuvil et al., 2005; Sevrioukov et al., 1999; Takáts et al., 2014; Takáts et al., 2015; Warner et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The loss of proteins required for early endosomal fusions (such as Vps8, Vps16a, Vps18, Vps33a and Rabenosyn-5) leads to the fragmentation of Rab7 positive late endosomes in garland nephrocytes.
source: Briefly, the loss of proteins required for early endosomal fusions (such as Vps8, Vps16a, Vps18, Vps33a and Rabenosyn-5) leads to the fragmentation of Rab7 positive late endosomes, while the loss of late endosomal-lysosomal tether HOPS (Vps11, Vps41, Vps39) leads to the enlargement of Rab7 positive endosomes (Lőrincz et al., 2016a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: The loss of late endosomal-lysosomal tether HOPS (Vps11, Vps41, Vps39) leads to the enlargement of Rab7 positive endosomes in garland nephrocytes.
source: Briefly, the loss of proteins required for early endosomal fusions (such as Vps8, Vps16a, Vps18, Vps33a and Rabenosyn-5) leads to the fragmentation of Rab7 positive late endosomes, while the loss of late endosomal-lysosomal tether HOPS (Vps11, Vps41, Vps39) leads to the enlargement of Rab7 positive endosomes (Lőrincz et al., 2016a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Due to the accumulation of late endosomes, garland nephrocytes lacking HOPS are enlarged compared to control cells.
source: Due to the accumulation of late endosomes, these cells are also enlarged compared to control cells (Lőrincz et al., 2016a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Vps8 and Vps41 are suggested to occupy the same binding site in CORVET and HOPS, respectively.
source: As Vps8 and Vps41 are suggested to occupy the same binding site in CORVET and HOPS, respectively (Peplowska et al., 2007), we tested whether the overexpression of a complex specific subunit may result in the inhibition of the other complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Competition may exist between the CORVET and HOPS complex specific subunits in yeast.
source: In support of this model, yeast data suggested that competition may exist between the CORVET and HOPS complex specific subunits (Markgraf et al., 2009; Ostrowicz et al., 2010; Peplowska et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Vps8 overproducing garland nephrocytes are swollen.
source: Strikingly, we found that – similar to vps11 or vps39 RNAi cells - Vps8 overproducing cells are swollen (even in a Vps8 mutant background) and contain enlarged late endosomes based on both confocal and electron microscopy (Figure 1A–D,F–I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal and electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Vps8 overproducing garland nephrocytes contain enlarged late endosomes.
source: Strikingly, we found that – similar to vps11 or vps39 RNAi cells - Vps8 overproducing cells are swollen (even in a Vps8 mutant background) and contain enlarged late endosomes based on both confocal and electron microscopy (Figure 1A–D,F–I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal and electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The Vps8 overexpression phenotype in garland nephrocytes resembles the yeast data where Vps8 overexpression delayed late endosome maturation and caused the accumulation of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) proximal to the vacuole.
source: Importantly this phenotype resembles to the yeast data: Vps8 overexpression delayed late endosome maturation and caused the accumulation of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) proximal to the vacuole (Markgraf et al., 2009) and the overproduction of Vps3 (yeast specific CORVET subunit) caused vacuole fragmentation (Peplowska et al., 2007), which is a definitive characteristic of HOPS loss-of function in yeast cells (Raymond et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The overproduction of Vps3 (yeast specific CORVET subunit) caused vacuole fragmentation in yeast.
source: Importantly this phenotype resembles to the yeast data: Vps8 overexpression delayed late endosome maturation and caused the accumulation of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) proximal to the vacuole (Markgraf et al., 2009) and the overproduction of Vps3 (yeast specific CORVET subunit) caused vacuole fragmentation (Peplowska et al., 2007), which is a definitive characteristic of HOPS loss-of function in yeast cells (Raymond et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Vacuole fragmentation is a definitive characteristic of HOPS loss-of function in yeast cells.
source: Importantly this phenotype resembles to the yeast data: Vps8 overexpression delayed late endosome maturation and caused the accumulation of multivesicular bodies (MVBs) proximal to the vacuole (Markgraf et al., 2009) and the overproduction of Vps3 (yeast specific CORVET subunit) caused vacuole fragmentation (Peplowska et al., 2007), which is a definitive characteristic of HOPS loss-of function in yeast cells (Raymond et al., 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: In both metazoan and yeast cells, the overproduction of CORVET-specific subunits may interfere with HOPS function.
source: These data suggest that in both metazoan and yeast cells, the overproduction of CORVET-specific subunits may interfere with HOPS function.
evidence: This claim is based on the comparison of Drosophila data with yeast data from the literature.

claim: Vps8 overexpression in Drosophila completely phenocopied HOPS loss-of-function and apparently blocked late endosome to lysosome fusion.
source: First, Vps8 overexpression in Drosophila completely phenocopied HOPS loss-of-function and apparently blocked late endosome to lysosome fusion, unlike only causing a delay of endosome maturation observed in yeast.
evidence: This claim is based on the observation that Vps8 overexpression phenotypes are indistinguishable from HOPS loss-of-function phenotypes.

claim: Vps8 overexpression in yeast only causes a delay of endosome maturation.
source: First, Vps8 overexpression in Drosophila completely phenocopied HOPS loss-of-function and apparently blocked late endosome to lysosome fusion, unlike only causing a delay of endosome maturation observed in yeast.
evidence: This claim is based on cited yeast data.

claim: Vps8 overproduction caused punctate accumulation of Vps21 (Rab5 equivalent in yeast) on membranes in a Vps3-dependent fashion in yeast.
source: Second, Vps8 overproduction caused punctate accumulation of Vps21 (Rab5 equivalent in yeast) on membranes in a Vps3-dependent fashion (Peplowska et al., 2007) and MVBs in Vps8 overexpressing cells were also Vps21 positive (Markgraf et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: MVBs in Vps8 overexpressing yeast cells were Vps21 positive.
source: Second, Vps8 overproduction caused punctate accumulation of Vps21 (Rab5 equivalent in yeast) on membranes in a Vps3-dependent fashion (Peplowska et al., 2007) and MVBs in Vps8 overexpressing cells were also Vps21 positive (Markgraf et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: CORVET specific Vps proteins promote Vps21 localization in yeast cells.
source: These suggest that CORVET specific Vps proteins promote Vps21 localization in yeast cells.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on cited yeast data.

claim: Rab5 positive endosomes kept their peripheral localization in Vps8 overexpressing fly cells just like in HOPS depleted cells.
source: In contrast, Rab5 positive endosomes kept their peripheral localization in Vps8 overexpressing fly cells just like in HOPS depleted cells (Figure 1A–D), suggesting that in higher eukaryotes, (mini)CORVET is dispensable for the targeting and stability of Rab5 on endosomal membranes.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1.

claim: In higher eukaryotes, (mini)CORVET is dispensable for the targeting and stability of Rab5 on endosomal membranes.
source: In contrast, Rab5 positive endosomes kept their peripheral localization in Vps8 overexpressing fly cells just like in HOPS depleted cells (Figure 1A–D), suggesting that in higher eukaryotes, (mini)CORVET is dispensable for the targeting and stability of Rab5 on endosomal membranes.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that Rab5 localization is unaffected by Vps8 overexpression.

claim: Vps41-9xHA overexpression had no effect on garland cell or late endosome size.
source: To our surprise this was not the case, as Vps41-9xHA overexpression had no effect on garland cell or late endosome size (Figure 1A,E, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,E–G), changes in which are evident during Vps8 loss-of-function.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Vps41-9xHA expression completely rescued the Vps41 mutant phenotype.
source: Importantly, Vps41-9xHA expression completely rescued the Vps41 mutant phenotype: the size of both the cells and their late endosomes was similar to controls.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Vps41-9xHA signal could be detected on Rab7-positive endosomes.
source: Moreover, the Vps41-9xHA signal could be detected on Rab7-positive endosomes, together indicating that functional protein is expressed from the vps41-9xHA transgene (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: GFP-Vps41 localized to late endosomes and vacuole contact sites in yeast.
source: In line with this, GFP-Vps41 localized to late endosomes and vacuole contact sites in yeast, and the overexpression of Vps41 did not cause obvious defects, aside from a mild impairment of the AP-3 pathway (Cabrera et al., 2010; Cabrera et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The overexpression of Vps41 in yeast did not cause obvious defects, aside from a mild impairment of the AP-3 pathway.
source: In line with this, GFP-Vps41 localized to late endosomes and vacuole contact sites in yeast, and the overexpression of Vps41 did not cause obvious defects, aside from a mild impairment of the AP-3 pathway (Cabrera et al., 2010; Cabrera et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: If competition occurs between the complex specific subunits, then (mini)CORVET specific one(s) may have higher affinity towards class C Vps proteins than HOPS specific Vps protein(s) do in metazoan cells.
source: These together suggest that if competition occurs between the complex specific subunits, then (mini)CORVET specific one(s) may have higher affinity towards class C Vps proteins than HOPS specific Vps protein(s) do in metazoan cells.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observation that Vps8 overexpression inhibits HOPS but Vps41 overexpression does not inhibit miniCORVET.

claim: The larval fat tissue of Drosophila is a widely used model to study autophagy.
source: The larval fat tissue of Drosophila is a widely used model to study this process, and several established tools are available to monitor autophagy in flies (Lőrincz et al., 2017a; Mauvezin et al., 2014; Nagy et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The larval fat tissue of intensively growing (feeding) larvae is practically devoid of acidic lysosomes.
source: The larval fat tissue of intensively growing (feeding) larvae is practically devoid of acidic lysosomes, while starvation induces numerous bright lysotracker positive autolysosomes during an autophagy response (Lőrincz et al., 2017a; Scott et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Starvation induces numerous bright lysotracker positive autolysosomes during an autophagy response in larval fat tissue.
source: The larval fat tissue of intensively growing (feeding) larvae is practically devoid of acidic lysosomes, while starvation induces numerous bright lysotracker positive autolysosomes during an autophagy response (Lőrincz et al., 2017a; Scott et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The number of lysotracker positive lysosomes dramatically decreased in Vps8 overexpressing clone cells compared to surrounding control cells in mosaic animals.
source: We found that the number of lysotracker positive lysosomes dramatically decreased in Vps8 overexpressing clone cells (marked by the co-expression of GFP) compared to surrounding control cells in mosaic animals, indicating the impairment of starvation-induced autophagy (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Vps8 overexpressing cells are almost devoid of bright autolysosomes.
source: This reporter revealed that similar to vps39 RNAi cells, Vps8 overexpressing cells are indeed almost devoid of bright autolysosomes, only 'clouds' of many faint autophagosomes could be detected around the nuclei (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: Vps8 overproducing cells contained an elevated number of Atg8a dots.
source: Again similar to starved vps39 RNAi cells, Vps8 overproducing cells contained an elevated number of Atg8a dots (Figure 2D,E), indicating a defect in autophagic flux.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2D,E.

claim: There was no difference in the pattern of 3xmCherry-Atg8a or endogenous Atg8a signal between starved control and vps8 RNAi cells.
source: We could find no difference in the pattern of 3xmCherry-Atg8a or endogenous Atg8a signal between starved control and RNAi cells, indicating that in higher eukaryotes Vps8 - CORVET may not be involved in autophagy (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In higher eukaryotes Vps8/CORVET may not be involved in autophagy.
source: We could find no difference in the pattern of 3xmCherry-Atg8a or endogenous Atg8a signal between starved control and RNAi cells, indicating that in higher eukaryotes Vps8 - CORVET may not be involved in autophagy (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that Vps8 loss has no effect on autophagy markers.

claim: Expressing vps8 RNAi constructs in garland nephrocytes of genomic promoter-driven Vps8-9xHA expressing animals abolished the HA signal in these cells and phenocopied the loss of Vps8.
source: Importantly, expressing the same RNAi constructs in garland nephrocytes of genomic promoter-driven Vps8-9xHA expressing animals abolished the HA signal in these cells and phenocopied the loss of Vps8 as these cells were swollen and filled with small fragmented late endosomes in case of both RNAi lines (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Vps8 null mutant nephrocytes were indistinguishable from controls regarding punctate Atg8a and p62 signals.
source: At the same time, Vps8 null mutants were indistinguishable from controls regarding punctate Atg8a and p62 signals (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: HOPS-specific subunit mutants for Vps41/Lt and Vps11 as well as the class C Vps16A caused an obvious increase in the number of both Atg8a and p62 dots in nephrocytes.
source: HOPS-specific subunit mutants for Vps41/Lt and Vps11 as well as the class C Vps16A caused an obvious increase in the number of both Atg8a and p62 dots, indicating a block of autophagosome turnover (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,C–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Organism-wide overexpression of Vps8 led to an obvious upregulation of p62 and both forms of Atg8a in well-fed adult flies.
source: We then returned to Vps8 gain-of-function experiments and analyzed autophagic flux, that is, the turnover of material to be degraded. Organism-wide overexpression of Vps8 led to an obvious upregulation of p62 and both forms of Atg8a in well-fed adult flies, indicating a block of autophagic turnover (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The overexpression of Vps8 prevented the quenching of GFP in the mCherry-GFP-Atg8a reporter.
source: Compared to controls, the overexpression of Vps8 prevented the quenching of GFP: small dots double positive for both GFP and mCherry accumulated in starved fat cells (Figure 3A,B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), indicating defective autophagic flux.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The overlap of 3xmCherry-Atg8a with GFP-Lamp1 signals dramatically decreased upon Vps8 overexpression.
source: In controls, large 3xmCherry dots are positive for GFP-Lamp1 indicating ongoing fusions of autophagosomes with lysosomes, but the overlap of these signals dramatically decreased upon Vps8 overexpression (Figure 3C,D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Vps8 overexpression impairs autophagosome-lysosome fusion.
source: These suggest the impairment of autophagosome-lysosome fusion in Vps8 overexpressing cells, causing autophagosomes and small lysosomes to accumulate.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that autophagosomes and lysosomes do not fuse in Vps8 overexpressing cells.

claim: The size of the lysosomal marker dLamp-3xmCherry positive dots decreased and their number increased in starved Vps8 overproducing cells.
source: Accordingly, the size of the lysosomal marker dLamp-3xmCherry positive dots decreased and their number increased in starved Vps8 overproducing cells, similar to Rab7-positive structures that represent both autophagosomes and lysosomes in these cells (Hegedűs et al., 2016) (Figure 4A,C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

claim: vps8 RNAi had no effect on the dLamp-3xmCherry or Rab7 pattern.

claim: The main ultrastructural characteristic of developmental autophagy in fat cells is the appearance of very large electron dense (auto)lysosomes.

claim: The ultrastructure of Vps8 overexpressing fat cells shows no large lysosomes but numerous small lysosomes and autophagosomes fill the cytoplasm.

evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Overexpression of Vps8 inhibits autophagosome-lysosome fusion via the loss of HOPS.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that overexpression of Vps8 inhibits autophagosome-lysosome fusion via the loss of HOPS, which also impaired both starvation-induced and developmental autophagy in flies (Takáts et al., 2014).

claim: Both yeast and mammalian HOPS complexes are required for autophagosome clearance.
source: As both yeast and mammalian HOPS complexes are required for autophagosome clearance (McEwan et al., 2015; Rieder and Emr, 1997), it will be interesting to test whether the overexpression of CORVET specific subunits also affects autophagy and related processes in these organisms.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: HOPS is essential for lysosome related organelle biogenesis that includes the pigment granules of the fly compound eyes.
source: For example, HOPS is essential for lysosome related organelle biogenesis that includes the pigment granules of the fly compound eyes: several classical eye pigmentation mutants have been shown to carry mutations in genes encoding HOPS subunits (Lloyd et al., 1998; Lőrincz et al., 2016b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Several classical eye pigmentation mutants have been shown to carry mutations in genes encoding HOPS subunits.
source: For example, HOPS is essential for lysosome related organelle biogenesis that includes the pigment granules of the fly compound eyes: several classical eye pigmentation mutants have been shown to carry mutations in genes encoding HOPS subunits (Lloyd et al., 1998; Lőrincz et al., 2016b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: 5-day-old Vps8 overexpressing adults had darker eyes compared to age-matched controls.

claim: The pseudopupil was completely absent in Vps8 overexpressing eyes.

claim: The Vps8 overexpression eye phenotype is remarkably similar to the phenotype of animals homozygous for the lt1 classical eye color mutant.

evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Crinophagy is an atg gene-independent special autophagic process in which excess secretory granules directly fuse with lysosomes in a HOPS-dependent manner.
source: Crinophagy is an atg gene-independent special autophagic process in which excess secretory granules directly fuse with lysosomes in a HOPS-dependent manner (Csizmadia et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Larval salivary glands are an excellent model to study crinophagy.
source: Larval salivary glands are an excellent model to study crinophagy because at the beginning of metamorphosis, excess glue protein containing secretory granules are broken down this way.

claim: Glue-GFP but not Glue-dsRed is quenched inside acidic crinosomes of control or vps8 RNAi cells.
source: Similar to mCherry-GFP-Atg8a autophagic flux reporters, Glue-GFP but not Glue-dsRed is quenched inside acidic crinosomes of control or vps8 RNAi cells, but GFP signal persists in Vps8 overexpressing cells (Figure 5A,B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C), indicating the impairment of crinophagy.

claim: GFP signal persists in Vps8 overexpressing salivary gland cells.

evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 5.

claim: At the onset of crinophagy, the lysosomal membrane protein GFP-Lamp1 forms 'rings' around granules designated for degradation upon glue granule-lysosome fusion.
source: At the onset of crinophagy, the lysosomal membrane protein GFP-Lamp1 forms 'rings' around granules designated for degradation upon glue granule-lysosome fusion, but in Vps8 overexpressing cells no rings are formed: instead, GFP-Lamp1 shows punctate pattern as a result of a fusion defect between lysosomes and secretory granules (Figure 5C,D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 5.

claim: In Vps8 overexpressing salivary gland cells no GFP-Lamp1 rings are formed.
source: At the onset of crinophagy, the lysosomal membrane protein GFP-Lamp1 forms 'rings' around granules designated for degradation upon glue granule-lysosome fusion, but in Vps8 overexpressing cells no rings are formed: instead, GFP-Lamp1 shows punctate pattern as a result of a fusion defect between lysosomes and secretory granules (Figure 5C,D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The Vps8 overexpression phenotype in salivary glands is indistinguishable from HOPS loss-of function.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Vps41-9xHA clearly overlapped with endogenous Rab7 at the rim of late endosomes in garland nephrocytes.
source: As expected, Vps41-9xHA clearly overlapped with endogenous Rab7 at the rim of late endosomes in garland nephrocytes (Figure 6A, see also Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).

claim: Vps41-9xHA localized only to a sub-population of Rab7 positive endosomes but not to lysosomes.
source: Interestingly, Vps41-9xHA localized only to a sub-population of Rab7 positive endosomes but not to lysosomes (although adjacent CathL and Vps41-9xHA positive organelles were often seen), and sometimes only a Vps41-9xHA patch could be detected on the late endosomes (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).

claim: Vps41 defines a novel late endosomal compartment in nephrocytes.
source: Thus, Vps41 defines a novel late endosomal compartment in nephrocytes: 598/1739 of the Rab7 endosomes (34.02%) were Vps41-9xHA positive based on the analysis of 52 cells from nine animals, suggesting that only mature endosomal membranes (ready to fuse with lysosomes) acquire Vps41/HOPS in order to avoid premature fusion.

claim: 34.02% of Rab7 endosomes were Vps41-9xHA positive based on the analysis of 52 cells from nine animals.
source: Thus, Vps41 defines a novel late endosomal compartment in nephrocytes: 598/1739 of the Rab7 endosomes (34.02%) were Vps41-9xHA positive based on the analysis of 52 cells from nine animals, suggesting that only mature endosomal membranes (ready to fuse with lysosomes) acquire Vps41/HOPS in order to avoid premature fusion.

claim: Only mature endosomal membranes (ready to fuse with lysosomes) acquire Vps41/HOPS in order to avoid premature fusion.

claim: Vps41 association with a subset of late endosomes in nephrocytes is lost upon Vps8 overexpression.
source: Vps41 association with a subset of late endosomes in nephrocytes (Figure 6A,F) is lost upon Vps8 overexpression: Vps41-9xHA becomes dispersed in the cytoplasm and accumulates in the nucleus in these cells (Figure 6B,F, Figure 6—figure supplement 2D).

claim: Vps41-9xHA becomes dispersed in the cytoplasm and accumulates in the nucleus upon Vps8 overexpression.
source: Vps41 association with a subset of late endosomes in nephrocytes (Figure 6A,F) is lost upon Vps8 overexpression: Vps41-9xHA becomes dispersed in the cytoplasm and accumulates in the nucleus in these cells (Figure 6B,F, Figure 6—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The late endosomal localization of Vps41-9xHA is lost upon HOPS-specific (vps39 or vps11) or class C (vps18, vps16A or vps33A) RNAi.
source: Importantly, the late endosomal localization of Vps41-9xHA is also lost upon HOPS-specific (vps39 or vps11) or class C (vps18, vps16A or vps33A) RNAi (Figure 6A,C–F, Figure 6—figure supplement 2B–D), suggesting that Vps41 can associate to target membranes only as part of the fully assembled HOPS complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Vps41 can associate to target membranes only as part of the fully assembled HOPS complex.
source: Importantly, the late endosomal localization of Vps41-9xHA is also lost upon HOPS-specific (vps39 or vps11) or class C (vps18, vps16A or vps33A) RNAi (Figure 6A,C–F, Figure 6—figure supplement 2B–D), suggesting that Vps41 can associate to target membranes only as part of the fully assembled HOPS complex.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that Vps41 localization depends on all other HOPS subunits.

claim: Vps41-9xHA retains its late endosomal, Rab7-associated localization in vps8 loss-of-function cells.
source: Of note, Vps41-9xHA retains its late endosomal, Rab7-associated localization in vps8 loss-of-function cells (Figure 6E,F, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A), indicating that miniCORVET has no role in promoting Vps41 recruitment to target membranes.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6.

claim: miniCORVET has no role in promoting Vps41 recruitment to target membranes.
source: Of note, Vps41-9xHA retains its late endosomal, Rab7-associated localization in vps8 loss-of-function cells (Figure 6E,F, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A), indicating that miniCORVET has no role in promoting Vps41 recruitment to target membranes.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that Vps41 localization is unaffected by Vps8 loss.

claim: HOPS has been shown to be involved in the AP-3 pathway in yeast.
source: HOPS has been shown to be involved in the AP-3 pathway in yeast (Angers and Merz, 2009) and human Vps41 was suggested to regulate TGN to late endosome transport, possibly as an AP-3 coat in a HOPS independent manner (Pols et al., 2013b).

claim: Human Vps41 was suggested to regulate TGN to late endosome transport, possibly as an AP-3 coat in a HOPS independent manner.
source: HOPS has been shown to be involved in the AP-3 pathway in yeast (Angers and Merz, 2009) and human Vps41 was suggested to regulate TGN to late endosome transport, possibly as an AP-3 coat in a HOPS independent manner (Pols et al., 2013b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Vps41 functions predominantly as part of HOPS in Drosophila nephrocytes.
source: Vps41-9xHA no longer associates to endosomes upon HOPS or class C loss and its distribution becomes mostly diffuse in these cells, suggesting that Vps41 functions predominantly as part of HOPS in Drosophila nephrocytes.
evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that Vps41 localization depends on HOPS assembly.

claim: Both Vps41 and Vps39 are equally required for targeting lysosomal membrane proteins from the TGN to endosomes.
source: In line with this, a recent study showed that both Vps41 and Vps39 are equally required for targeting lysosomal membrane proteins from the TGN to endosomes (Lund et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Vps8 (miniCORVET) localization to early endosomes relies on Rab5 but not Rab7.
source: We have previously shown that Vps8 (miniCORVET) localization to early endosomes relies on Rab5 but not Rab7 (Lőrincz et al., 2016a), which motivated us to carry out functional analyses of selected small GTPases to identify additional factors required for Vps41/HOPS targeting.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Rab2 directly binds to the Vps39 end of HOPS.
source: We have recently shown that Rab2 directly binds to the Vps39 end of HOPS, and Rab7 is also important for HOPS function even though it may bind this tethering complex only indirectly in Drosophila (Lőrincz et al., 2017b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Rab7 is important for HOPS function even though it may bind this tethering complex only indirectly in Drosophila.
source: We have recently shown that Rab2 directly binds to the Vps39 end of HOPS, and Rab7 is also important for HOPS function even though it may bind this tethering complex only indirectly in Drosophila (Lőrincz et al., 2017b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Lysosomal Arl8/Gie has been identified as a HOPS binding small GTPase in Drosophila and human cells.
source: In addition, lysosomal Arl8/Gie has also been identified as a HOPS binding small GTPase in Drosophila and human cells (Khatter et al., 2015; Rosa-Ferreira et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Knockdown of either rab7 or rab2 leads to the cytoplasmic dispersion of Vps41-9xHA.
source: Indeed, we found that knockdown of either rab7 or rab2 leads to the cytoplasmic dispersion of Vps41-9xHA, and Vps41-9xHA association with vesicles positive for these Rabs in cells expressing their GTP bound (thus presumably constitutively active) YFP tagged mutant forms was increased compared to control cells (Figure 7A–E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).

claim: Vps41-9xHA association with vesicles positive for Rab7 or Rab2 in cells expressing their GTP bound YFP tagged mutant forms was increased compared to control cells.
source: Indeed, we found that knockdown of either rab7 or rab2 leads to the cytoplasmic dispersion of Vps41-9xHA, and Vps41-9xHA association with vesicles positive for these Rabs in cells expressing their GTP bound (thus presumably constitutively active) YFP tagged mutant forms was increased compared to control cells (Figure 7A–E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Occasional Vps41 rings were still observed in rab7 RNAi cells.
source: Interestingly, occasional Vps41 rings were still observed in rab7 RNAi cells, in line with our model that it is Rab2 that directly binds HOPS and may be more important for its recruitment.
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Rab2 directly binds HOPS and may be more important for its recruitment than Rab7.
source: Interestingly, occasional Vps41 rings were still observed in rab7 RNAi cells, in line with our model that it is Rab2 that directly binds HOPS and may be more important for its recruitment.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observation that some Vps41 rings persist in rab7 RNAi cells.

claim: Ultrastructural analysis showed that rab7 RNAi cells contain numerous enlarged endosomes and abnormal lysosomes just like HOPS depleted cells.
source: Of note, ultrastructural analysis showed that rab7 RNAi cells contain numerous enlarged endosomes and abnormal lysosomes (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E) just like HOPS depleted cells (Figure 1H,I), indicating that the mostly cytosolic localization of Vps41 is not due to the absence of endosomes, but it is a consequence of the absence of Rab7 itself.

claim: The mostly cytosolic localization of Vps41 in rab7 RNAi cells is not due to the absence of endosomes, but it is a consequence of the absence of Rab7 itself.
source: Of note, ultrastructural analysis showed that rab7 RNAi cells contain numerous enlarged endosomes and abnormal lysosomes (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E) just like HOPS depleted cells (Figure 1H,I), indicating that the mostly cytosolic localization of Vps41 is not due to the absence of endosomes, but it is a consequence of the absence of Rab7 itself.

claim: Vps41-9xHA still retains its late endosomal association in Arl8/Gie depleted cells, although its overlap with Rab7 rings decreases.
source: Interestingly, Vps41-9xHA still retains its late endosomal association in Arl8/Gie depleted cells, although its overlap with Rab7 rings decreases (Figure 7F, Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7.

claim: In rab5 depleted cells that are devoid of Rab7 positive vesicles, Vps41 is dispersed in the cytoplasm.

claim: Cells expressing GTP-locked YFP-Rab5 contain numerous double Rab5 and Rab7 positive hybrid vesicles and Vps41-9xHA is never recruited to these.

evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

evidence: This claim is an inference based on the observation that Vps8 and Vps41 localize to different compartments.

claim: The association of Vps41 and Vps39 to membranes is required for the stability of HOPS in yeast.
source: Since the association of Vps41 and Vps39 to membranes is required for the stability of HOPS in yeast (Cabrera et al., 2009; Ostrowicz et al., 2010) and Vps18 recruits Vps41 to the human HOPS complex (Hunter et al., 2017), we reasoned that the amount of assembled HOPS may decrease upon Vps8 overproduction.

claim: Vps18 recruits Vps41 to the human HOPS complex.
source: Since the association of Vps41 and Vps39 to membranes is required for the stability of HOPS in yeast (Cabrera et al., 2009; Ostrowicz et al., 2010) and Vps18 recruits Vps41 to the human HOPS complex (Hunter et al., 2017), we reasoned that the amount of assembled HOPS may decrease upon Vps8 overproduction.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Vps41-9xHA is found in the Drosophila HOPS complex.
source: We found that in controls, Vps41-9xHA readily co-immunoprecipitated endogenous Vps16A, Vps18 and Vps33A, indicating that Vps41-9xHA is found in the Drosophila HOPS complex (Figure 8).
evidence: This claim is an inference based on co-immunoprecipitation data.
